title: Walk the multiplier up on dust
teach: A raise is a sign test, not a size test: any epoch that closes positive counts, however little put it there. Six one-wei buys, one per epoch, walk the multiplier from its launch value to its ceiling — six wei in total, against a hundred-ETH pool. The ceiling is not sticky, though: cuts are immediate and five times larger than raises, so one quiet epoch gives back five epochs of work. See test/A3.test.ts, which measures the whole walk.

expect.notesYellow: Six wei, one per epoch, took the multiplier from 1.00 to its 1.25 ceiling. Nothing was round-tripped, so none of it paid the spread that the adversarial probes measure against an 80 ETH pump — a strategy that moves no size has nothing to slip. Holding the ceiling costs another wei per epoch; missing one epoch costs 0.25, which is five raises.
